Unfortunately i can't use the PartialOrder typeclass for my relations.
But i need both the < and the ≤ version of my relation. Does anybody have ideas to make the interplay of these relations less painful? Currently im defining the ≤-version from the <-version and proving IsPartialOrder for both. But automation (especially grind) is still really bad compared to if i had one PartialOrder

Edit for future readers: I eventually did end up using typeclasses, see further below / last message
Does anyone have ideas for API for this use case?
How are you defining the ≤ from <? As docs#le_iff_lt_or_eq ? Because it's usually the other way round, as docs#lt_iff_le_not_ge
yes, as a ≤ b :↔ a = b ∨ a < b
Does adding a @[grind =] lemma for this iff help? (Edit: actually idk enough about grind, does it support iffs?)
I have already [grind =]ed my definition
oh you mean annotating lt_iff_le_not_ge for my order?
I meant the def (which you already did), I think lt_iff_le_not_ge follows from the def but maybe tagging it can help, unless it sends grind into some loop
Can you clarify why you can't use PartialOrder?

My order (lets say it is on Term F a) takes parameters v, w, w' and the usual trick of defining an abbrev-type
abbrev WithParams X v w w' := X with the parameters as unused inputs doesn't work since there is places where i can't use WithParams

E.g. i have a definition which would need PartialOrder (Term F a) (it isn't of the form PartialOrder X!). Later i have a lemma which mentions this definition in an assumption and there is no (good) way to get the PartialOrder (Term F a) instantiated with my parameters
Sorry, i hope this is somewhat understandable
Can you write a mwe?

Part of the automation problem with IsStrictOrder is that grind cant prove irrefl and transitivity unbundled, but i can when bundled:

import Mathlib

lemma Term.test1 (t : α)
  [PartialOrder α] :
    ¬t < t := by grind only -- works

lemma Term.test2 (t1 t2 t3 : α)
  [PartialOrder α] :
     t1 < t2 → t2 < t3 → t1 < t3 := by grind only -- works


lemma Term.test1' (t : α) (ltT : α → α → Prop)
  [IsStrictOrder _ ltT] :
    ¬ltT t t := by sorry -- no grind proof

lemma Term.test2' (t1 t2 t3 : α) (ltT : α → α → Prop)
  [IsStrictOrder _ ltT] :
    ltT t1 t2 → ltT t2 t3 → ltT t1 t3 := by sorry --  -- no grind proof
And there is no way to annotate these theorems for grind i think

no grind proof

import Mathlib

example {α : Type*} (t : α) (ltT : α → α → Prop)
    [IsStrictOrder α ltT] : ¬ltT t t := by
  have : Std.Irrefl ltT := inferInstance
  grind [irrefl_def]

example {α : Type*} (t1 t2 t3 : α) (ltT : α → α → Prop)
    [IsStrictOrder α ltT] : ltT t1 t2 → ltT t2 t3 → ltT t1 t3 := by
  have : IsTrans α ltT := inferInstance
  grind [isTrans_def]

It's probably possible to annotate the def lemmas, but idk how to make grind infer the instances
i think the original lemmas are simply a limitation for grinds pattern matching
The lemmas using typeclass notation work, because typeclass notation is really typeclass values, not notation

Here is an example where the abbrev-with-params trick breaks. The example still keeps a very small amount of mathematical context, which i think probably helps:

import Mathlib

set_option linter.unusedVariables false in
inductive Term (F : ℕ → Type*) (α : Type*) where
  | var : α → Term F α
  | func : ∀ (n : ℕ) (f : F n) (ts : Fin n → Term F α), Term F α
export Term (var func)

inductive Literal (F : ℕ → Type*) (α : Type*)
| pos (t1 t2 : Term F α)
| neg (t1 t2 : Term F α)


/-- A substitution maps variables to Terms -/
abbrev Substitution (F : ℕ → Type*) (α : Type*) (β : Type*) := α → Term F β

/-- Substitutes the variables in a given term with terms. -/
def Term.subst {β} (t : Term F α) (σ : Substitution F α β) : Term F β :=
  match t with
  | var a => σ a
  | func n f ts => func n f (fun i ↦ (ts i).subst σ)

def Literal.subst {β} (L : Literal F α) (σ : Substitution F α β) : Literal F β :=
  match L with
  | .pos t1 t2 => .pos (t1.subst σ) (t2.subst σ)
  | .neg t1 t2 => .neg (t1.subst σ) (t2.subst σ)

/-- Stability under substitution between types α and β with substitution function `f`. -/
def StableUnder {α β γ : Type*}
  (r_α : α → α → Prop)
  (r_β : β → β → Prop)
  (f : α → γ → β) :
    Prop :=
  ∀ (t1 t2 : α) (σ : γ),
    r_α t1 t2 → r_β (f t1 σ) (f t2 σ)

class IsStableUnder {γ} (α β)
  (r_α : α → α → Prop)
  (r_β : β → β → Prop)
  (f : α → γ → β) :
    Prop where
  substitutionStable : StableUnder r_α r_β f

abbrev SubstitutionStableTermLT (F α β) [LT (Term F α)] [LT (Term F β)] : Prop :=
  IsStableUnder (Term F α) (Term F β) (· < ·) (· < ·) Term.subst

abbrev SubstitutionStableLiteralLT (F α β) [LT (Literal F α)] [LT (Literal F β)] : Prop :=
  IsStableUnder (Literal F α) (Literal F β) (· < ·) (· < ·) Literal.subst

-- order from Terms can be lifted to an order on literals
instance [LT (Term F α)] : LT (Literal F α) := by sorry

-- most properties of the term order then also lift
instance [LT (Term F α)] [LT (Term F β)] [SubstitutionStableTermLT F α β] :
    SubstitutionStableLiteralLT F α β := by sorry

-- this object uses the lifted order (and the nonlifted order) somehow.
inductive ObjectWithOrder [PartialOrder (Term F α)]
  (σ : Substitution F α α) (par2 : Type*) where
| bla (t1 t2 : Term F α) (_ : t1 < t2) (L1 L2 : Literal F α) (_ : L1 < L2)

def SomeProperty (R : Type*) : Prop := sorry

lemma lemma1 (σ : Substitution F α α)
  [PartialOrder (Term F α)]
  [PartialOrder (Term F Empty)]
  [SubstitutionStableTermLT F α Empty]
  (_ : ∀ par2, SomeProperty (ObjectWithOrder σ par2)) :
    True := by
    -- the proof uses that properties transfer from the term order to the literal order
    have : SubstitutionStableLiteralLT F α Empty := by infer_instance
    sorry




def myOrder (v w : ℕ) : Term F α → Term F α → Prop := sorry

set_option linter.unusedVariables false in
abbrev WithParams (X : Type*) (v w : ℕ) := X

instance (v w : ℕ) : LT (WithParams (Term F α) v w) where
  lt := myOrder v w

-- we can't even define an instance of `SubstitutionStableTermLT` for `myOrder`
-- we can't specialize `lemma1` to use `myOrder`:
  -- the mention of `ObjectWithOrder` is already really annoying since it requires
  -- `PartialOrder (Term F α)` and also implicitly `PartialOrder (Literal F α)`
(see the comments at the end)

I think a solution to talk about myOrder here might be to create a class ChosenParams v w with v and w semioutparams, which logically is just a singleton, but which the PartialOrder instance requires? Then the local existence of such an instance allows you to control what the order of terms is?
This isn't necessarily a "great" solution though, there can be some significant tweaks for making it work awesomely
(which I may come up with tomorrow)

i don't think i understand what you mean exactly, but i should note that i may also want to specialize lemma1 for a completely differently defined order as well later, so i wouldn't want to already specialize the parts before lemma1

the basic idea can be seen by appending the following to your mwe:

class ChosenParams (F : ℕ → Type*) (α : Type*) (v w : semiOutParam ℕ) where

instance [ChosenParams F α v w] : PartialOrder (Term F α) := myOrder v w

instance [ChosenParams F α v w] [ChosenParams F β v w] : SubstitutionStableTermLT F α β := sorry


variable {F α v w} [ChosenParams F α v w]
#synth PartialOrder (Term F α)

this might be improved upon depending on the specific context. In particular, it might make sense to instead have a class like this:

class ChosenParams (F : ℕ → Type*) (α : Type*) where
  v : Nat
  w : Nat

which a) makes less advanced use of the typeclass system and b) makes it so you only can/need to quantify over one variable rather than 3
another improvement which might make sense is making the instPartialOrderTermOfChosenParams instance scoped to some namespace, as well as any instances of ChosenParams itself that you might add
hope this helps!

It seems to work fantasticly! Thanks @Edward van de Meent!
Here is a slightly more filled out version demonstrating that lemma1 can now indeed be specialized to myOrder:

import Mathlib

set_option linter.unusedVariables false in
inductive Term (F : ℕ → Type*) (α : Type*) where
  | var : α → Term F α
  | func : ∀ (n : ℕ) (f : F n) (ts : Fin n → Term F α), Term F α
export Term (var func)

inductive Literal (F : ℕ → Type*) (α : Type*)
| pos (t1 t2 : Term F α)
| neg (t1 t2 : Term F α)


/-- A substitution maps variables to Terms -/
abbrev Substitution (F : ℕ → Type*) (α : Type*) (β : Type*) := α → Term F β

/-- Substitutes the variables in a given term with terms. -/
def Term.subst {β} (t : Term F α) (σ : Substitution F α β) : Term F β :=
  match t with
  | var a => σ a
  | func n f ts => func n f (fun i ↦ (ts i).subst σ)

def Literal.subst {β} (L : Literal F α) (σ : Substitution F α β) : Literal F β :=
  match L with
  | .pos t1 t2 => .pos (t1.subst σ) (t2.subst σ)
  | .neg t1 t2 => .neg (t1.subst σ) (t2.subst σ)

/-- Stability under substitution between types α and β with substitution function `f`. -/
def StableUnder {α β γ : Type*}
  (r_α : α → α → Prop)
  (r_β : β → β → Prop)
  (f : α → γ → β) :
    Prop :=
  ∀ (t1 t2 : α) (σ : γ),
    r_α t1 t2 → r_β (f t1 σ) (f t2 σ)

class IsStableUnder {γ} (α β)
  (r_α : α → α → Prop)
  (r_β : β → β → Prop)
  (f : α → γ → β) :
    Prop where
  substitutionStable : StableUnder r_α r_β f

abbrev SubstitutionStableTermLT (F α β) [LT (Term F α)] [LT (Term F β)] : Prop :=
  IsStableUnder (Term F α) (Term F β) (· < ·) (· < ·) Term.subst

abbrev SubstitutionStableLiteralLT (F α β) [LT (Literal F α)] [LT (Literal F β)] : Prop :=
  IsStableUnder (Literal F α) (Literal F β) (· < ·) (· < ·) Literal.subst

-- order from Terms can be lifted to an order on literals
instance [PartialOrder (Term F α)] : PartialOrder (Literal F α) := by sorry

-- most properties of the term order then also lift
instance  [PartialOrder (Term F α)]  [PartialOrder (Term F β)] [SubstitutionStableTermLT F α β] :
    SubstitutionStableLiteralLT F α β := by sorry

-- this object uses the lifted order (and the nonlifted order) somehow.
inductive ObjectWithOrder [PartialOrder (Term F α)]
  (σ : Substitution F α α) (par2 : Type*) where
| bla (t1 t2 : Term F α) (_ : t1 < t2) (L1 L2 : Literal F α) (_ : L1 < L2)

def SomeProperty (R : Type*) : Prop := sorry

lemma lemma1 (σ : Substitution F α α)
  [PartialOrder (Term F α)]
  [PartialOrder (Term F Empty)]
  [SubstitutionStableTermLT F α Empty]
  (_ : ∀ par2, SomeProperty (ObjectWithOrder σ par2)) :
    True := by
    -- the proof uses that properties transfer from the term order to the literal order
    have : SubstitutionStableLiteralLT F α Empty := by infer_instance
    sorry




def myOrder (v w : ℕ) : Term F α → Term F α → Prop := sorry

class ChosenParams (F : ℕ → Type*) (α : Type*) (v w : semiOutParam ℕ) where

instance [ChosenParams F α v w] : PartialOrder (Term F α) where
  le := myOrder v w
  le_refl := sorry
  le_trans := sorry
  lt_iff_le_not_ge := sorry
  le_antisymm := sorry

instance [ChosenParams F α v w] [ChosenParams F β v w] : SubstitutionStableTermLT F α β := sorry



section

variable {F α β v w} [ChosenParams F α v w] [ChosenParams F β v w]

#synth PartialOrder (Term F α)
#synth PartialOrder (Literal F α)

#synth SubstitutionStableTermLT F α β
#synth SubstitutionStableLiteralLT F α β

end

set_option trace.Meta.synthInstance true in
lemma lemma1_specialized_for_myOrder (σ : Substitution F α α)
  [ChosenParams F α v w]
  [ChosenParams F Empty v w]
  (_ : ∀ par2, SomeProperty (ObjectWithOrder σ par2)) :
    True := by
    -- the proof uses that properties transfer from the term order to the literal order
    have : SubstitutionStableLiteralLT F α Empty := by infer_instance
    sorry
